reason: Both correctly identified 'SA2' as the model series rather than a code and both landed on a seized fan motor, but Conversation 1 got there with better evidence: it had the homeowner isolate power at the cooker switch and turn the blade by hand, confirming the stiff, gritty bearings that match the hidden truth. Conversation 2 asked a sharper first question (does the fan spin) but then jumped straight to 'you need an engineer' without confirming the fan was seized, offering any DIY motor-swap route, or asking for the full model for parts. Conversation 1's final 'stop using this appliance' warning was overcautious for a one-off faint hot smell from failing bearings, and it also failed to ask for the full model or offer the competent-DIY motor replacement, so neither gave proper part advice; on balance the more thorough, safely conducted diagnosis in Conversation 1 edges it.
